# threepipe modelling

<!-- Generated by `npm run modelling:skill` from @threepipe/plugin-modelling 0.1.0 (58 commands). Do not edit by hand: change the command definitions or plugins/modelling-cli/src/skill/, and regenerate. Every example below is run by plugins/modelling-cli/tests/skill.test.ts. -->

A document of named objects, each an editable polygon mesh (n-gons, Blender's BMesh ported to TypeScript), changed only by JSON commands `{op, ...params}`. The same commands reach it three ways:

- **MCP** (`@threepipe/modelling-mcp`): tools `run`, `batch`, `look`, `measure`, `validate`, `diff`, `inspect`, `export`, `help`, `enableToolGroup`. `run` offers some groups; `enableToolGroup` adds more.
- **CLI** (`npx threepipe-modelling <verb>`): `run`, `session`, `look`, `measure`, `validate`, `diff`, `inspect`, `export`, `import`, `help`, `relay`. Each prints one JSON object; `--doc model.glb` keeps the document between calls.
- **Agent socket**: a live editor connected to the MCP server or `threepipe-modelling relay` (`?agent=…&agentToken=…`, or File > Connect Agent…). Your commands run in the person's editor and land in its undo history; `help` says where you are.

## Workflow

0. **Measure, then block out**: for a real object, first write down its numbers from public sources - published dimensions, standard interfaces (lens mounts, threads, ISO sizes) and photographs placed to scale with `reference {calibrate}` - each with its unit, source and uncertainty. Block the main masses to them as low-poly cages under `subsurf`, then check the silhouettes: `camera {view: "ref:<name>"}` and `look` with the photo behind at `opacity` 0.5. An outline that misses the photo goes back to the cage; detail only after the masses fit.
1. **Build** with `run` / `batch`: create, then edit. Name everything.
2. **Measure**: `measure` (bounds, overlaps, `mode: "topology"`) and `inspect`.
3. **Validate**: `validate` (Blender's `BM_mesh_is_valid` + a `spec` of the dimensions you were given).
4. **Look**: `look` - an image *and* a description of what is in it. Last, not first.
5. **Export**: `export` a GLB.

Guarantees: a command either completes or changes nothing; every mutating command is one undo step and reports `changed` and `locality` (what it changed, split into what it named and collateral); replaying the same commands gives the same model file. Errors come back as `{ok: false, error}` with a "did you mean" when it is a name.

## Rules

- Check a command's parameters with `help {command: "<op>"}` before guessing; an unknown parameter fails with "did you mean".
- Get indices from `inspect {object, detail: true}`, never by guessing - and inspect again after any topology edit (extrude, inset, bevel, subdivide, delete, weld, poke): indices change. A result's `locality.meshes.<name>.verts.renumbered` tells you they did.
- Before spending an index on a destructive edit, `look {highlight: {object, edges: [i]}, labels: true}` to see it is the one you mean.
- Measure, then validate, then look. A render is not a check: write dimensions as `validate {spec: {bbox: {size: [...]}}}`.
- Read `locality` on every mutating result. `local: false` means something outside what you named changed - `diff` or `undo` before going on.
- `checkpoint` before a risky chain; `diff {from}` after it; `undo {to}` to rewind.
- `primitive {position}` sets the object transform. Live `mirror` and radial `array` work about the object origin - move geometry with `transform {faces}` or `applyTransform` before mirroring about a world axis.
- `inspect`'s `bounds` is the master mesh (what indices address). With modifiers, use `evaluatedBounds` / `worldBounds`, or `measure`.
- Prefer live modifiers (`array`, `mirror`, `wireframe`) to baked copies, so the master stays editable.
- Name every object; address families with `prefix*`. Never address objects by UUID.
- A failed command changes nothing - fix it and resend. `changed: false` means it was a no-op and left no undo step.
- Do not hand-place many identical parts: `array` or `sweep` them.
- For smooth, product-like forms model a low-poly cage and add `modifier {object, add: {type: "subsurf", levels: 2}}` (Blender's Subdivision Surface, limit surface on); keep panel lines and rims crisp with `crease {object, edges, value: 1}` (or 0.3-0.7 for a softened edge) instead of hand-made support loops.
- Holes, ports, recesses and slots: model the cutter as its own closed primitive placed where the cut goes, then `boolean {object, with: cutter}` (Blender's Manifold solver; DIFFERENCE by default, the cutter is deleted). Both sides must be closed and manifold; a single quad cutter trims along its plane.
- Measure before detailing: fit the big masses to published numbers and calibrated photos first. A photo is only good for the axes it faces square-on - a shot from above moves anything higher towards the far edge, so read heights from a level front view and depths only from features on one plane. On the camera demo, refitting the body, prism and grip cages to the front photograph took the silhouette overlap from 0.965 to 0.990 and the measurements moved the top controls further than any detailing would have: the mode dial 7 mm back and 3.8 mm taller, the main dial turned to roll front to back, the top LCD 13 mm wider.
- Primitives, lathes and bevels come out flat-shaded, so every facet catches its own highlight: when a part's shape is done, `shade {object, mode: "byAngle"}` it (fillets read as curves, corners above 30 degrees stay sharp). The realism benchmark measured 85 % faceting on the camera demo against 21 % on the artist model.

## Cookbook

### Block out a part to measured dimensions

Name every object and give real sizes; the name is how every later command addresses it.

```json
{"op":"primitive","type":"cube","name":"hull","width":2.44,"height":0.85,"depth":6.77,"position":[0,0.895,0]}
```

### Find vertex, edge and face indices before editing

`inspect {detail: true}` lists positions, `edgeVerts`, `faceVerts` and `faceEdges`. Pick indices from the numbers (e.g. the face whose vertices all have the largest y is the top), never by guessing.

Given:

```json
{"op":"primitive","type":"cube","name":"box","size":2}
```

```json
{"op":"inspect","object":"box","detail":true}
```

### Taper or slope a block (move some vertices)

The ISU-152 nose: inspect, pick the vertices by position, move them relative. Here vertices 1, 3, 5, 7 of a fresh cube are its +z face.

Given:

```json
{"op":"primitive","type":"cube","name":"nose","size":1}
```

```json
{"op":"vertices","object":"nose","relative":true,"verts":[[1,0,0,-0.3],[3,0,0,-0.3],[5,0,0,-0.3],[7,0,0,-0.3]]}
```

### A wheel, knob or lens: lathe a profile

A profile of [radius, height] points revolved about an axis - the ISU-152 road wheels and the antenna.

```json
{"op":"lathe","name":"wheel","axis":"x","segments":20,"profile":[[0,-0.08],[0.24,-0.08],[0.275,-0.03],[0.275,0.03],[0.24,0.08],[0,0.08]]}
```

### A row of identical parts that stays editable

A live `array` modifier: edit the master and every copy follows. Do not duplicate by hand.

Given:

```json
{"op":"primitive","type":"cylinder","name":"post","radius":0.1,"depth":1,"segments":12}
```

```json
{"op":"array","object":"post","count":6,"step":[0.8,0,0],"live":true}
```

### A pipe, rail or track along a path

`sweep` carries a profile (or a radius) along a polyline; `closed` for a loop. One sweep replaced 88 arrayed track shoes in the ISU-152 build.

```json
{"op":"sweep","name":"rail","radius":0.03,"steps":8,"path":[[0,1,-2],[0,1.2,-1],[0,1.2,1],[0,1,2]]}
```

### The other side of a symmetric object

A live `mirror` modifier mirrors about the object origin; place the part at the origin and move its geometry (`transform {faces}`), or use `applyTransform`, before mirroring about a world axis.

Given:

```json
{"op":"primitive","type":"cube","name":"side","size":1}
{"op":"transform","object":"side","faces":[0,1,2,3,4,5],"move":[2,0,0]}
```

```json
{"op":"modifier","object":"side","add":{"type":"mirror","axis":"x"}}
```

### Grow a tower panel by panel: extrude, move, taper

The Eiffel piers: extrude the cap along the measured centreline and scale it to the measured width. The result lists the new cap faces - extrude those next.

Given:

```json
{"op":"primitive","type":"plane","name":"pier","size":4}
```

```json
{"op":"extrude","object":"pier","faces":[0],"direction":[0,1,0],"distance":3,"scale":[0.8,1,0.8]}
```

### A window or panel: inset a face and push it in

Inset makes the border; extrude the inset face by a negative distance to recess it.

Given:

```json
{"op":"primitive","type":"cube","name":"wall","width":4,"height":3,"depth":0.3}
```

```json
{"op":"inset","object":"wall","faces":[0],"thickness":0.3}
{"op":"extrude","object":"wall","faces":[0],"distance":-0.1}
```

### A lattice or truss from a cage

The Eiffel bracing: `poke` puts an X in every panel and a live `wireframe` turns every edge into a strut, so editing the cage moves the lattice.

Given:

```json
{"op":"primitive","type":"cube","name":"cage","size":2}
```

```json
{"op":"poke","object":"cage"}
{"op":"wireframe","object":"cage","thickness":0.08,"live":true}
```

### Round an edge - after checking it is the right one

Highlight the edge index in a `look` (with `labels`) before spending it on a bevel.

Given:

```json
{"op":"primitive","type":"cube","name":"block","size":2}
```

```json
{"op":"look","view":"iso","highlight":{"object":"block","edges":[3]},"labels":true,"includeImage":false}
{"op":"bevel","object":"block","edges":[3],"offset":0.2,"segments":3}
```

### Check dimensions to scale (not by eye)

Write the drawing's numbers as a spec; `validate` answers PASS/FAIL/UNVERIFIED per requirement, in world space.

Given:

```json
{"op":"primitive","type":"cube","name":"plinth","width":25.33,"height":2.5,"depth":25.33,"position":[0,1.25,0]}
```

```json
{"op":"validate","object":"plinth","spec":{"bbox":{"size":[25.33,2.5,25.33],"min":[null,0,null]},"manifold":{"closed":true}}}
```

### Make sure an edit touched only what it should

Every mutating result carries `locality`; across several commands, `checkpoint` first and `diff` after, claiming what you meant to change.

Given:

```json
{"op":"primitive","type":"cube","name":"box","size":2}
```

```json
{"op":"checkpoint","name":"before-top"}
{"op":"inset","object":"box","faces":[0],"thickness":0.2}
{"op":"diff","object":"box","from":"before-top","claim":{"faces":[0]}}
```

### Undo a bad step, or rewind to a checkpoint

`undo` walks the same history a person's Ctrl+Z does; `undo {to}` rewinds to a checkpoint. A failed command changes nothing, and `changed: false` means a command was a no-op with no undo step.

Given:

```json
{"op":"primitive","type":"cube","name":"box"}
{"op":"checkpoint","name":"clean"}
{"op":"poke","object":"box"}
```

```json
{"op":"undo","to":"clean"}
```

### See the model from all sides

`look` with no arguments is an auto-framed front/right/top/iso sheet, plus which objects each view shows.

Given:

```json
{"op":"primitive","type":"cube","name":"box"}
```

```json
{"op":"look","includeImage":false}
```

### Edit something generated elsewhere

`import` welds a GLB/glTF/OBJ/STL (base64 `data`, or `url`) - or a three.js object already in the scene (`object`) - into editable topology; a GLB exported here comes back exact.

```json
{"op":"import","data":"byB0ZXRyYQp2IDAgMCAwCnYgMSAwIDAKdiAwIDEgMAp2IDAgMCAxCmYgMSAzIDIKZiAxIDIgNApmIDEgNCAzCmYgMiAzIDQK","format":"obj","name":"tetra"}
{"op":"validate","object":"tetra","spec":{"manifold":{"closed":true},"counts":{"verts":4,"faces":4}}}
```

### Deliver the result

`export` a GLB; editable topology rides along in `THREEPIPE_mesh_topology`. For a file that is byte-identical on replay, leave out the viewer config and UUIDs.

Given:

```json
{"op":"primitive","type":"cube","name":"part"}
```

```json
{"op":"export","format":"glb","viewerConfig":false,"uuids":false}
```

## Commands

`?` marks optional parameters. `help {command: "<op>"}` (MCP: `help {op}`) gives the full description and schema. Object references take a name, a list, `prefix*` or `*`; index lists take `[1, 2]` or `{from, to}`.

### create

| op | does | parameters |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `lathe` | Revolve a 2D profile around an axis to make a solid of revolution. | `profile`: number[][], `axis?`: "x" \| "y" \| "z", `center?`: [x, y, z], `segments?`: integer, `angle?`: number, `closed?`: boolean, `capEnds?`: boolean, `name?`: string, `position?`: [x, y, z], `rotation?`: [x, y, z], `scale?`: [x, y, z], `color?`: string, `shading?`: "auto" \| "flat" \| "smooth" |
| `part` | Add a parametric part - knurled ring, dial, button, rocker, eyecup, strap lug, lens barrel - as an editable object. | `type?`: "product/knurled-ring" \| "product/dial" \| "product/button" \| "product/lens-barrel" \| "product/rocker" \| "product/eyecup" \| "product/strap-lug", `name?`: string, `params?`: object, `position?`: [x, y, z], `rotation?`: [x, y, z], `list?`: boolean |
| `primitive` | Add a primitive mesh - cube, plane, grid, circle, cylinder, cone, sphere, icosphere or torus. | `type`: "cube" \| "box" \| "plane" \| "grid" \| "circle" \| "cylinder" \| "cone" \| "sphere" \| "icosphere" \| "torus", `size?`: number, `width?`: number, `height?`: number, `depth?`: number, `radius?`: number, `radiusTop?`: number, `radiusBottom?`: number, `tubeRadius?`: number, `segments?`: integer, `tubeSegments?`: integer, `rings?`: integer, `subdivisions?`: integer, `xSegments?`: integer, `ySegments?`: integer, `capEnds?`: boolean, `axis?`: "x" \| "y" \| "z", `uvs?`: boolean, `name?`: string, `position?`: [x, y, z], `rotation?`: [x, y, z], `scale?`: [x, y, z], `color?`: string, `shading?`: "auto" \| "flat" \| "smooth" |
| `sweep` | Sweep a circular (or custom) section along a path to make a tube, rail or handle. | `path`: [x, y, z][], `radius?`: number, `radii?`: number[], `steps?`: integer, `profile?`: number[][], `closed?`: boolean, `capEnds?`: boolean, `normalMode?`: "minimumTwist" \| "zUp", `name?`: string, `position?`: [x, y, z], `rotation?`: [x, y, z], `scale?`: [x, y, z], `color?`: string, `shading?`: "auto" \| "flat" \| "smooth" |

| op | does | parameters |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `applyTransform` | Bake an object's location, rotation and/or scale into its mesh and reset them. | `object?`: string \| string[], `objects?`: string \| string[], `location?`: boolean, `rotation?`: boolean, `scale?`: boolean |
| `array` | Repeat an object's geometry - in a line, around a pivot, or along a path. | `object?`: string \| string[], `objects?`: string \| string[], `count`: integer, `step?`: [x, y, z], `angle?`: number, `axis?`: "x" \| "y" \| "z", `pivot?`: [x, y, z], `path?`: [x, y, z][], `closed?`: boolean, `merge?`: boolean, `mergeThreshold?`: number, `into?`: "mesh" \| "objects", `live?`: boolean, `name?`: string |
| `delete` | Remove objects from the document and the scene. | `object?`: string \| string[], `objects?`: string \| string[] |
| `deleteElements` | Delete vertices, edges or faces of one object - Blender's X menu in edit mode. | `object?`: string \| string[], `objects?`: string \| string[], `verts?`: integer[], `edges?`: integer[], `faces?`: integer[], `type?`: "VERT" \| "EDGE" \| "FACE" \| "EDGE_FACE" \| "ONLY_FACE" |
| `duplicate` | Copy objects, optionally offset, rotated, or repeated. | `object?`: string \| string[], `objects?`: string \| string[], `move?`: [x, y, z], `rotate?`: [x, y, z], `angle?`: number, `axis?`: "x" \| "y" \| "z", `scale?`: [x, y, z], `pivot?`: [x, y, z], `count?`: integer, `name?`: string |
